name: Red Hat Enterprise Linux
install: ISO installer; free for personal development use via the Red Hat Developer Subscription
desc: RHEL is the distribution the RHCSA and RHCE exams are set on. A Developer Subscription is free for personal use and gives you the real thing rather than a rebuild.

name: Rocky Linux
desc: Rocky Linux is a community rebuild that is binary-compatible with RHEL, making it a free stand-in for exam practice.

name: AlmaLinux
desc: AlmaLinux is a foundation-backed, binary-compatible RHEL rebuild, the other common free choice for RHCSA labs.

name: Fedora
desc: Fedora is Red Hat's upstream community distribution, useful for seeing where RHEL features are heading.

name: Debian
desc: Debian is a stable, widely deployed general-purpose distribution and the base for many others.

name: Ubuntu Server
desc: Ubuntu Server is the most common Linux target in cloud images and a frequent choice for self-hosting labs.

name: FreeBSD
desc: FreeBSD is a complete Unix-like operating system developed as a single coherent base, used heavily in networking and storage appliances.

name: OpenBSD
desc: OpenBSD is a Unix-like system with a strong focus on correctness and security, and the origin of OpenSSH and PF.

name: Cockpit
desc: Cockpit is a browser-based administration console for Linux servers, covering services, storage, networking and logs. It ships with RHEL and is worth knowing for RHCSA.

name: Ansible
install: pip install ansible  or  dnf install ansible-core
desc: Ansible is the agentless automation tool the current RHCE exam is built around. The control node is Linux-only, so run it from a lab VM or WSL.

name: AWX
install: Deploy with the AWX Operator on Kubernetes
desc: AWX is the upstream open-source project behind Ansible Automation Platform's web UI, API, and job scheduling.

name: Docker Engine
install: Follow the distribution instructions in the upstream docs
desc: Docker Engine is the container runtime and daemon on Linux hosts, as distinct from Docker Desktop on a workstation.

name: Kubernetes
install: kubeadm, k3s, or a managed cloud service
desc: Kubernetes is the container orchestration platform the CKA, CKAD and CKS exams are set on. Practise against a real cluster, not only a local one.

name: Rancher
desc: Rancher manages multiple Kubernetes clusters from one control plane, with centralised authentication and policy.

name: Portainer
desc: Portainer is a lightweight web UI for managing Docker and Kubernetes environments, popular in home labs.

name: Prometheus
desc: Prometheus is the de facto open-source metrics and alerting system, scraping time-series data from instrumented targets.

name: Grafana Loki
desc: Loki is a log aggregation system designed to index labels rather than full log text, pairing with Grafana for queries.

name: Graylog
desc: Graylog is a centralised log management platform with parsing, search, dashboards and alerting.

name: Elasticsearch
desc: Elasticsearch is the search and analytics engine underpinning the ELK stack, widely used for log and security analytics.

name: Uptime Kuma
desc: Uptime Kuma is a self-hosted uptime monitor with status pages and a wide range of notification channels.

name: Cisco Packet Tracer
install: Free download, but only through a Cisco Networking Academy account
desc: Packet Tracer is Cisco's network simulator and the standard CCNA study tool. There is no public package: you must register with Networking Academy to download it.

name: GNS3
desc: GNS3 emulates real network topologies using actual device images and containers, going well beyond what a simulator can model. You supply your own licensed IOS images.

name: EVE-NG
install: Import the OVA into a hypervisor
desc: EVE-NG is a clientless network emulation platform you run as a virtual appliance, used for large multi-vendor lab topologies.

name: Containerlab
desc: Containerlab builds network topologies from containerised routing images declaratively, a modern alternative to GUI emulators for automation practice.

name: pfSense
install: ISO installer on dedicated hardware or a VM
desc: pfSense is a FreeBSD-based firewall and router distribution with VPN, traffic shaping and a web interface.

name: OPNsense
install: ISO installer on dedicated hardware or a VM
desc: OPNsense is a FreeBSD-based firewall platform, forked from pfSense, with a strong release cadence and plugin system.

name: VyOS
install: ISO installer; rolling builds are free
desc: VyOS is a Linux-based network operating system with a unified CLI, useful for practising routing configuration without vendor hardware.

name: MikroTik RouterOS
install: Vendor download; CHR runs free in a VM with a speed limit
desc: RouterOS is MikroTik's router operating system. The Cloud Hosted Router image runs in a VM, so you can practise real routing and firewalling cheaply.

name: LibreNMS
desc: LibreNMS is an auto-discovering network monitoring system using SNMP, with alerting and multi-vendor support.

name: Nagios Core
desc: Nagios Core is a long-established host and service monitoring system built around check plugins.

name: Zabbix Server
desc: Zabbix is an enterprise monitoring platform for networks, servers and applications. The Windows agent in this directory reports to a server like this one.

name: NetBox
desc: NetBox is the standard open-source source of truth for network documentation: IPAM, racks, circuits, devices and cabling.

name: phpIPAM
install: Docker, or a PHP web server
desc: phpIPAM is a lightweight, web-based IP address management tool with subnet scanning and VLAN tracking.

name: Asterisk
desc: Asterisk is the open-source telephony engine behind a great many VoIP and SIP deployments.

name: FreePBX
install: ISO installer, or on top of an existing Asterisk host
desc: FreePBX is a web configuration layer over Asterisk, turning it into a manageable PBX for VoIP labs.

name: Kali Linux
desc: Kali is the penetration-testing distribution that bundles the toolset most offensive-security courses assume. Running it as a VM is how you get Metasploit, sqlmap, hashcat and the rest on a Windows machine.

name: Parrot Security OS
desc: Parrot Security is a Debian-based security distribution, an alternative to Kali with a lighter desktop and a privacy focus.

name: Security Onion
desc: Security Onion is a monitoring distribution that bundles Suricata, Zeek, Elasticsearch and Kibana into a working network security monitoring stack.

name: REMnux
install: VM appliance, or an install script on Ubuntu
desc: REMnux is a Linux toolkit curated for reverse-engineering and analysing malicious software.

name: Tails
install: Write the image to a USB stick
desc: Tails is an amnesic live operating system that routes traffic through Tor and leaves no trace on the host disk.

name: Qubes OS
desc: Qubes OS enforces security by compartmentalising your work into separate virtual machines by trust level.

name: Metasploit Framework
install: Bundled with Kali, or the vendor installer
desc: Metasploit is the standard exploitation and post-exploitation framework. Use it only against systems you own or are authorised in writing to test.

name: Ghidra
install: Download the release archive and run; requires a JDK
desc: Ghidra is the NSA's software reverse-engineering suite, with a decompiler that made serious binary analysis free. It runs on Windows but ships as an archive, not a package.

name: hashcat
install: Download the release archive; needs GPU drivers
desc: hashcat is a GPU-accelerated password recovery tool used for auditing password strength against recovered hashes. Audit only hashes you are authorised to test.

name: John the Ripper
install: Bundled with Kali, or build from source
desc: John the Ripper is a long-standing password-cracking tool used for auditing weak credentials.

name: sqlmap
desc: sqlmap automates detection and exploitation of SQL injection flaws. Point it only at applications you are authorised to test.

name: Nikto
desc: Nikto is a web server scanner that checks for dangerous files, outdated versions and configuration problems.

name: THC Hydra
install: Bundled with Kali, or build from source
desc: Hydra is a parallelised network login cracker supporting many protocols, used to demonstrate weak credential policies in authorised tests.

name: Aircrack-ng
install: Bundled with Kali, or the vendor build
desc: Aircrack-ng is a suite for assessing Wi-Fi network security, covering capture, analysis and key recovery. Test only networks you own.

name: Responder
desc: Responder is an LLMNR, NBT-NS and MDNS poisoner used in authorised internal assessments to demonstrate credential-relay exposure.

name: Impacket
desc: Impacket is a collection of Python classes for working with network protocols, widely used for Windows and Active Directory testing.

name: BloodHound
install: Docker Compose for the server; collectors run on the domain
desc: BloodHound maps Active Directory attack paths as a graph, used by both red teams and the AD administrators hardening against them.

name: Greenbone / OpenVAS
install: Docker, or the Greenbone Community appliance
desc: Greenbone Vulnerability Management, built on the OpenVAS scanner, is the main open-source alternative to commercial vulnerability scanners.

name: Lynis
desc: Lynis audits the security configuration of a Unix-like host and reports hardening suggestions with references.

name: OpenSCAP
desc: OpenSCAP evaluates a system against SCAP security policies such as CIS and DISA STIG baselines, and ships in RHEL.

name: TheHive
desc: TheHive is a security incident response platform for case management and collaborative investigation, often paired with MISP.

name: MISP
desc: MISP is a threat intelligence platform for storing, correlating and sharing indicators of compromise.

name: Volatility 3
desc: Volatility is the memory-forensics framework for extracting processes, network state and injected code from RAM captures. The Windows GUI in this directory wraps it.

name: CyberChef
install: Use the hosted page, or serve the static build yourself
desc: CyberChef is a browser-based tool for encoding, decoding, parsing and analysing data, invaluable for CTFs and incident triage.

name: Semgrep
desc: Semgrep is a fast static analysis tool for finding security bugs and enforcing code standards using pattern rules.

name: Prowler
desc: Prowler audits AWS, Azure, GCP and Kubernetes against security best practice and compliance benchmarks.

name: ScoutSuite
desc: ScoutSuite is a multi-cloud security auditing tool that produces an offline HTML report of configuration risk.

name: Zeek
install: Distribution packages, or build from source
desc: Zeek (formerly Bro) turns network traffic into rich structured logs rather than alerts, the backbone of serious network security monitoring.

name: Snort
desc: Snort is a signature-based intrusion detection and prevention system maintained by Cisco, with community and subscriber rule sets.

name: Proxmox VE
desc: Proxmox VE is a bare-metal hypervisor combining KVM virtual machines and LXC containers with clustering and backups, the usual choice for a serious home lab.

name: TrueNAS
desc: TrueNAS is a storage operating system built on ZFS, providing NAS and SAN services with snapshots and replication.

name: OpenMediaVault
install: ISO installer, or a script on Debian
desc: OpenMediaVault is a Debian-based NAS solution with a web interface and a plugin system, lighter than TrueNAS for small setups.

name: Nginx
install: Distribution packages, or the official repository
desc: Nginx is a high-performance web server, reverse proxy and load balancer, and one of the two servers most of the web runs on.

name: Apache HTTP Server
desc: The Apache HTTP Server is the long-established modular web server, and the one RHCSA-track material usually configures.

name: HAProxy
desc: HAProxy is a reliable, high-performance TCP and HTTP load balancer used in front of large deployments.

name: Traefik
desc: Traefik is a reverse proxy that discovers services automatically from Docker or Kubernetes and handles TLS certificates for them.

name: Certbot
desc: Certbot obtains and renews free Let's Encrypt TLS certificates and can configure your web server to use them.

name: BIND 9
desc: BIND is the reference DNS server implementation, still the standard way to learn authoritative and recursive DNS properly.

name: PowerDNS
desc: PowerDNS is a DNS server with pluggable database backends and a separate recursor, common in hosting environments.

name: Technitium DNS Server
desc: Technitium is a self-hostable DNS server with ad blocking, DoH and DoT support and a clear web interface, approachable for a home lab.

name: Mailcow
desc: Mailcow is a dockerised mail server suite bundling Postfix, Dovecot, Rspamd and a web UI. Running mail well is hard; this makes it tractable.

name: Mail-in-a-Box
install: Install script on a clean Ubuntu host
desc: Mail-in-a-Box turns a fresh Ubuntu server into a working mail server with DNS, webmail and spam filtering in one script.

name: Coolify
desc: Coolify is a self-hostable deployment platform, an open alternative to Heroku-style hosting for your own server.

name: Dokku
install: Install script on a Linux host
desc: Dokku is a minimal single-host platform-as-a-service built on Docker, deploying apps with a git push.

name: CapRover
desc: CapRover is a self-hosted PaaS with a web UI, one-click app store and automatic TLS, built on Docker Swarm.

name: HestiaCP
install: Install script on Debian or Ubuntu
desc: Hestia Control Panel is a lightweight open-source web hosting panel covering web, mail, DNS and databases.

name: CyberPanel
install: Install script on a supported distribution
desc: CyberPanel is a hosting control panel built on OpenLiteSpeed, with staging, backups and one-click WordPress.

name: Authentik
desc: Authentik is a self-hosted identity provider supporting SAML, OAuth2 and LDAP, giving single sign-on to your own services.

name: Keycloak
desc: Keycloak is Red Hat's open-source identity and access management server, handling SSO, federation and fine-grained authorisation.

name: BorgBackup
desc: Borg is a deduplicating, compressing, encrypted backup program for Unix-like systems, frequently paired with Borgmatic for scheduling.

name: Clonezilla
install: Write the live image to a USB stick
desc: Clonezilla is a bootable disk and partition imaging tool for bare-metal backup, restore and mass deployment.

name: GParted
install: Live USB image, or distribution packages
desc: GParted is a graphical partition editor, usually run from its live image to resize or repair partitions a running OS cannot touch.

name: OpenProject
desc: OpenProject is a self-hosted project management suite with work packages, Gantt charts, agile boards and time tracking.

name: Redmine
desc: Redmine is a long-established issue tracker and project management application with per-project wikis and forums.

name: Taiga
desc: Taiga is an agile project management tool built around Scrum and Kanban workflows.

name: Vikunja
desc: Vikunja is a self-hosted task and project manager with list, Gantt, table and Kanban views.

name: Plane
desc: Plane is an open-source project planning tool covering issues, cycles and modules, positioned as a Jira alternative.

name: Wekan
desc: Wekan is an open-source Kanban board, a straightforward self-hosted stand-in for Trello.
